title: School buildings can interrupt learning before their long-term effects are visible
source_unit: U.S. Government Accountability Office GAO-26-107970 nationwide survey and interviews on public school facility issues in school year 2024–25

denominator.unit: national public school district survey estimate universe described by GAO

districts_with_facility_cancellation.unit: percent of districts that canceled school for at least one day because of a facility issue

students_affected.unit: estimated students affected by facility-related cancellations

learning_days_affected.unit: estimated days of learning lost through reported facility-related cancellations

districts_with_chronic_facility_issue.unit: percent of districts with a chronic facility issue in at least one school

serious_facility_challenge.unit: percent of districts considering chronic facility problems a serious or very serious challenge to meeting facility needs

reported_disruption_types.value: plumbing emergencies and extreme classroom temperatures among leading reasons for cancellation

student_and_family_outcomes.unit: student learning, attendance recovery, health, family work/care disruption, repair effectiveness, and later opportunity

observations.method: GAO nationwide survey of public school districts, review of district reports, interviews with district leaders and officials, and selected site visits; national estimates are kept separate from student-level outcomes.
observations.uncertainty: The cancellation, student, and learning-day figures are survey-based estimates. The report does not measure actual learning loss, make-up instruction, student health, family burden, repair completion, or later outcomes at the individual level.
observations.subgroup: Public school districts and students affected by facility-related cancellations; selected district visits and interviews are not nationally generalizable for mechanisms.
observations.counterinterpretation: Closing a school can protect students from unsafe heat, plumbing, air, or other conditions, and districts may provide make-up instruction; a scheduled-day cancellation is not automatically a measured learning loss.

boundary: This record captures district-reported facility disruption and national estimates of affected students and learning days. It does not establish student-level learning loss, unequal causal effects, family income or care burden, repair effectiveness, public trust, or durable educational outcomes.
